page: Google Cloud Platform e2-highmem-2 is an x86_64 architecture instance belonging to the E2 server family. It features 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical Intel Xeon core with 2 threads per core, operating at a clock speed of 2.2 GHz. The memory configuration consists of 16.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. This instance does not include bundled local NVMe storage or GPU accelerators, and it provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates that the e2-highmem-2 operates in lower performance tiers across compute and memory subsystems. The single-core stress-ng CPU performance score is 1101.98, and the multi-core score is 1451.88, placing both in the bottom 25% and 10% respectively. Memory bandwidth tests show 80.53 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 12.0 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, reflecting limited throughput. Similarly, the Geekbench single-core score of 841.0 and multi-core score of 1028.0 align with the bottom 10% of tested instances.

The primary tradeoff of the e2-highmem-2 is its low compute and memory bandwidth performance relative to its generous 16.0 GB memory allocation. This resource density makes it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for workloads that require a larger memory footprint but have minimal CPU demands. Appropriate workloads include small-scale databases, memory-cached applications, lightweight web serving with static web serving throughput measured at 1.43 GB/sec, and basic text or image processing tasks.

Powered by a 2.2 GHz Intel Xeon processor with 1 physical core and 2 threads, this instance lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. Despite these performance limitations, the high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-dependent workloads with low CPU requirements. It is best suited for small databases, caching layers, and lightweight web serving.
